Subject: Beacon RFP – continuity questionnaire (initial clarifications)

Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. We reviewed the high-level section on disaster recovery and have a few clarifications before we move to the technical validation stage. The security & resilience team here needs the following in writing:

- RTO and RPO commitments for your hosted API vs. Dedicated (reserved) deployments. Please call out numbers by deployment type and by failure class (single-instance, AZ outage, region outage).

- Evidence or artifacts we can use for acceptance testing (runbooks, sample DR test report, timestamps from a prior failover rehearsal).

Beacon Insurance

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Alicia —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a compact appendix with numeric commitments, sequencing, and artifacts for acceptance testing. If helpful we can walk through the appendix on the call next week.

Summary (hosted API / Dedicated):
- RTO: Hosted API – 15 minutes (automatic region routing, warm-standby handoff within 15m). Dedicated – 30 minutes for full capacity failover (assuming reserved pool scaling and network promotion).
- RPO: Hosted API – near-zero for user-visible state (prefix/KV cache may be lost for in-flight sessions; durable logs are replicated across AZs with typical <60s lag). Dedicated – configurable to near-zero with synchronous replication; default is <5 minutes.
- Failure classes: single-node failure handled automatically via intra-cluster replacement (<1 minute for request reroute, recovery background). AZ outage triggers active routing to remaining AZ within 5–15 minutes depending on in-flight caching. Full region outage follows our warm-standby activation sequence and model routing fallback (15–30 minutes).

Switchover sequencing (summary):
1) Detection & triage: Automatic alarms + human verification (on-call SRE).
2) Pre-failover validation: Sanity checks and traffic count verification (SRE + account engineer).
3) Traffic routing change: Smart routing switches to standby region using health-check gating.
4) Capacity ramp & health validation: Gradual traffic increase with active telemetry and rollbacks if error budget breached.
5) Full cutover & postmortem: Formal RCA and acceptance test run.

Acceptance evidence we can provide:
- Runbook (runbook-activation-sequence.xlsx) with step-by-step ops commands.
- Appendix PDF with historical rehearsal timestamps and sample RTO measurement (beacon-RTO-RPO-appendix.pdf).
- Test harness logs and a redacted incident report from a 2026 rehearsal (redacted log excerpts included in appendix).

Escalation contacts & SLA exceptions:
- Primary on-call SRE: s-sre@redwood.com (24/7)
- Account escalation: marissa.cole@redwood.com
- Enterprise SLA lead: neha.kapoor@redwood.com

I attached the appendix and the runbook extract. Let us know three windows next week that work for your infra team and we’ll lock the walkthrough.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0126

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@beaconinsurance.com>

Rishi —

Thanks for the appendix. A couple of concrete clarifications we need before the walkthrough (so our infra team can prep):

1) You mention "warm-standby activation" with 15–30 minute RTO for region failures — can you confirm the 15m value applies to the hosted multi-region configuration with prefix/KV cache warm in a secondary region? If not, please call out the conditions (e.g., pre-warmed pool, last-mile DNS TTLs).
2) For Dedicated customers, is synchronous replication available across regions or only across AZs? If synchronous cross-region replication requires configuration, what is the opt-in impact on latency and cost?
3) For acceptance testing, we will require a playbook of the exact commands and a smoke-test checklist that our SREs can run to verify each step of traffic redirection and model correctness. Can you confirm those are included in the runbook spreadsheet?

Also: please confirm whether Redwood will provide a post-test signed summary with timestamps we can ingest into our test validation tracker.

If you can respond to the three points in-line, we’ll lock a slot for next Wednesday at 10:00 PT.

Appreciate it,
Alicia

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@beaconinsurance.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Beacon RFP – continuity questionnaire (initial clarifications) — proposed in-line responses

Marissa / Neha —

Looping you both for a quick sign-off on the in-line responses before the 10:00 PT walkthrough tomorrow. I drafted short, explicit answers below so Alicia can paste them into their tracker. Please review and flag any wording or SLA exposure you want tightened.

--- Quoted: Alicia's questions ---

1) Warm-standby activation / 15m RTO: Our 15-minute RTO estimate applies to the hosted multi-region configuration under the following conditions: secondary region is pre-warmed (reserved warm pool), KV/prefix warm-cache warm sync completed within prior 24h window, and DNS/edge TTLs set to <= 60s. If any of these prerequisites are not met (e.g., no pre-warmed pool), expected RTO increases to 30–45 minutes. We are proposing a standard pre-warmed configuration for enterprise customers by default.

2) Dedicated cross-region replication: Synchronous cross-region replication is available as an opt-in feature for Dedicated customers. It requires additional network peering and adds nominal write latency (typically 5–15ms depending on region pair) and an incremental cost (~+12–18% on compute/bandwidth). Default Dedicated deployment includes cross-AZ sync only; we recommend opt-in for Beacon if sub-minute RPO is required.

3) Acceptance playbook & signed summary: The runbook spreadsheet contains step-by-step ops commands (sheet named "ActivationSteps") and a smoke-test checklist (sheet named "Smoke-Checks"). We will run the test jointly and provide a post-test signed summary with timestamps, measured RTO/RPO values, and any anomalies. Redwood will also provide a redacted sample rehearsal report ahead of the test for your ingestion test.

Notes for you both: I kept the language permissive but explicit to avoid overcommitment. If you prefer to change any numeric phrasing (especially the 15m guarantee language) we should tighten to "target" or move to appendix with conditional clauses.

Happy to jump on a 15-minute prep call before Alicia's walkthrough if useful.

Thanks,
Rishi
